In mathematics a '''Dirac structure''' is a geometric structure generalizing both [[symplectic structure]]s and [[Poisson structure]]s, and having several applications to mechanics. It is based on the notion of the [[Dirac bracket]] constraint introduced by [[Paul Dirac]] and was first introduced by [[Theodore James Courant|Ted Courant]] and [[Alan Weinstein]].

== Linear Dirac structures ==
Let ''<math>V</math>'' be a real [[vector space]], and ''<math>V^*</math>'' its [[Dual space|dual]]. A (linear) ''Dirac structure'' on ''<math>V</math>'' is a [[linear subspace]] ''<math>D</math>'' of <math>V\times V^*</math> satisfying
* for all <math>(v,\alpha)\in D</math> one has <math>\left\langle\alpha,\,v\right\rangle=0</math>,
* ''<math>D</math>'' is maximal with respect to this property.
In particular, if ''<math>V</math>'' is finite dimensional, then the second criterion is satisfied if <math>\dim D = \dim V</math>. Similar definitions can be made for vector spaces over other fields.

An alternative (equivalent) definition often used is that <math>D</math> satisfies <math>D=D^\perp</math>, where orthogonality is with respect to the symmetric [[bilinear form]] on <math>V\times V^*</math> given by <math>\bigl\langle(v,\alpha),\,(u,\beta)\bigr\rangle = \left\langle\alpha,u\right\rangle + \left\langle\beta,v\right\rangle</math>.

=== Examples ===
<ol><li>If <math>U\subset V</math> is a vector subspace, then <math>D=U\times U^\circ</math> is a Dirac structure on <math>V</math>, where <math>U^\circ</math> is the annihilator of <math>U</math>; that is, <math>U^\circ=\left\{\alpha\in V^*\mid \alpha_{\vert U}=0\right\}</math>.</li>

<li>Let <math>\omega:V\to V^*</math> be a skew-symmetric linear map, then the graph of <math>\omega</math> is a Dirac structure. </li>
<li>Similarly, if <math>\Pi:V^*\to V</math> is a skew-symmetric linear map, then its graph is a Dirac structure.</li>
</ol>

== Dirac structures on manifolds ==
A '''''Dirac structure''''' <math>\mathfrak{D}</math> on a [[smooth manifold]] ''<math>M</math>'' is an assignment of a (linear) Dirac structure on the tangent space to ''<math>M</math>'' at ''<math>m</math>'', for each <math>m \in M</math>. That is,
* for each <math>m\in M</math>, a Dirac subspace <math>D_m</math> of the space <math>T_mM\times T^*_mM</math>.
Many authors, in particular in geometry rather than the mechanics applications, require a Dirac structure to satisfy an extra ''integrability condition'' as follows:
* suppose <math>(X_i,\alpha_i)</math> are sections of the Dirac bundle <math>\mathfrak{D} \to M</math> (<math>i=1,2,3</math>) then <math>
\left\langle L_{X_1}(\alpha_2),\,X_3\right\rangle
+ \left\langle L_{X_2}(\alpha_3),\,X_1\right\rangle
+\left\langle L_{X_3}(\alpha_1),\,X_2\right\rangle = 0.
</math>

In the mechanics literature this would be called a ''closed'' or ''integrable'' Dirac structure.

=== Examples ===
<ol>
<li>Let <math>\Delta</math> be a [[Distribution (differential geometry)|smooth distribution]] of constant rank on a manifold ''<math>M</math>'', and for each <math>m\in M</math> let <math>D_m=\{(u,\alpha)\in T_mM\times T_m^*M \mid u\in\Delta(m),\,\alpha\in \Delta(m)^\circ\}</math>, then the union of these subspaces over ''<math>m</math>'' forms a Dirac structure on ''<math>M</math>''.
</li>
<li>Let <math>\omega</math> be a [[Symplectic manifold|symplectic form]] on a manifold <math>M</math>, then its graph is a (closed) Dirac structure. More generally, this is true for any closed 2-form. If the 2-form is not closed, then the resulting Dirac structure is not closed.
</li>
<li>Let <math>\Pi</math> be a [[Poisson structure]] on a manifold <math>M</math>, then its graph is a (closed) Dirac structure.
</li>
<li>Any submanifold of a Poisson manifold induces a Dirac structure.<ref>{{Citation |last=Bursztyn |first=Henrique |chapter=A brief introduction to Dirac manifolds |date=2013 |title=Geometric and Topological Methods for Quantum Field Theory: Proceedings of the 2009 Villa de Leyva Summer School |pages=4–38 |editor-last=Cardona |editor-first=Alexander |chapter-url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/geometric-and-topological-methods-for-quantum-field-theory/brief-introduction-to-dirac-manifolds/84FEC20910CB9E9A049B0C47CE874439 |place=Cambridge |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-107-02683-4 |editor2-last=Reyes-Lega |editor2-first=Andrés F. |editor3-last=Contreras |editor3-first=Iván}}</ref>
</li>
</ol>
